question.problem:
$$
{A}^{T}\,A=[\begin{aligned}73 & 24 \\ 24 & 9\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}{v}_{11} & {v}_{12} \\ {v}_{21} & {v}_{22}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the value of $|{v}_{11}|+|{v}_{21}|?$
question.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ the columns of $V$ must be the right singular vectors of $A,$ i.e., the unit eigenvectors of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=9$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=1.$ So, the first column of $V$ corresponds to the singular value ${\sigma }_{1}=9.$

Hence, we need to find a unit eigenvector of ${A}^{T}\,A$ that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=81.$ Computing ${A}^{T}\,A-81I,$ we get

$$
{A}^{T}\,A-81I=[\begin{aligned}73 & 24 \\ 24 & 9\end{aligned}]-81[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 24 \\ 24 & -72\end{aligned}]
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-81I)v=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we get 

$$
\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
|{v}_{11}|+|{v}_{21}|=|\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}|+|\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}|=\frac{4}{\sqrt{10}}.
$$
